circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has been the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One destination, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track situated around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside the Supercars Championship and various support events. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 licence for motorsport competition.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326-kilometre circuit originally operated as the Österreichring, hosting the Austrian Grand Prix annually from 1970 through 1987. Following significant modifications and renaming during the 1990s, the venue returned to Formula One hosting duties from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital that measures 6. 003 km per lap, ranking as the fourth-longest venue on the Formula One schedule. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before becoming a regular fixture on the calendar as the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and has hosted the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix annually, making it the venue for the sport's first Middle Eastern race. The Grade 1 FIA-licensed facility accommodates various racing categories including GP2 Series and endurance events, while featuring multiple configurable track layouts.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometres and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for various racing skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a Formula One venue since 1950 and currently hosts the Belgian Grand Prix, having held races annually since 1985 with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006. The track's history extends back to 1925 when it first hosted international motor racing competition.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, this 4. 361 km track serves as the permanent home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its primary use in elite single-seater racing, the circuit has accommodated various other prestigious motorsport categories including international sports car championships and North American touring series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019, with the event resuming from 2024 onward. The venue has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing competitions alongside its marquee Grand Prix fixture.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located in Northamptonshire, England, Silverstone Circuit is home to the British Grand Prix, which debuted there in 1948 and launched the inaugural World Championship of Drivers in 1950. After hosting the British Grand Prix intermittently with rival venues between 1955 and 1986, Silverstone became its permanent base from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km circuit near Budapest in Hungary, hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in the Eastern Bloc when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, making it the fastest Formula One circuit to construct, it was chosen over a proposed street layout in Budapest's central park after government preference for a purpose-built venue alongside a major highway.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. The venue has hosted the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, earning the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its notably long straights and fast-flowing corner design.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda Mobilityland. The track, accommodating up to 155,000 spectators, serves as a primary host for Formula One and Super Formula racing championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, weaving past the iconic hotels and casinos along Las Vegas Boulevard. The layout features some of the region's most recognizable venues, such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique urban racing environment.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two Mexican racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who both died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in multiple eras, returning to the championship calendar in 2015 on its current layout after a 23-year absence, and since 2021 the race carries the Mexico City Grand Prix designation.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, stretching 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and an average qualifying speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One racing, the venue joined the championship calendar in 2022 as the home of the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a short street course measuring 3. 337 kilometers that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, circling the harbour of the Principality of Monaco. The track is widely known as Monte Carlo, reflecting that most of its layout occupies the Monte Carlo neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch dunes near the North Sea coast, this 4. 259 km circuit hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix starting in 2021 after an absence from Formula One's calendar. The venue will conclude its current Formula One arrangement following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Located north of Doha in Qatar, the Lusail International Circuit is a 5. 419 km track featuring a 1. 068 km main straight and holds an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a Brazilian racing venue in São Paulo spanning 4. 309 km that opened in 1940 and runs in a counterclockwise direction. The circuit was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aircraft accident eight years earlier, and has housed his remains since 2024.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track located along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has served as the venue for the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural Formula One race in 2021. The circuit also began hosting a Formula E championship event in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing venue located in Singapore that winds around the Marina Bay area, incorporating sections through the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse cornering sequences, making it a versatile test for racing machinery. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home for the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track regularly hosts major international motorsport events including MotoGP's Americas round, the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, and NASCAR competitions, while previously accommodating various other series ranging from IndyCar to rallycross.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a dual Thai-British racing driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso represents Spain in Formula One competition for Aston Martin. The two-time world champion, who claimed his titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006, has accumulated 32 Grand Prix victories during his 23-season career. Beyond Formula One, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both Formula One and World Sportscar/World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian driver, made his Formula One debut in 2025 and has already secured six Grand Prix victories while racing for Mercedes.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabriel Bortoleto is a Brazilian Formula One driver currently racing for Audi in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his 13 seasons in the sport. He has achieved two runner-up finishes in the World Drivers' Championship with Mercedes and has secured 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian motorsport competitor, currently holds a reserve driver position with Haas while simultaneously racing in the European Le Mans Series LMP2 category for Nielsen Racing. He has made limited Formula One appearances, participating in seven Grand Prix events during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The AlphaTauri driver secured his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: British driver Lewis Hamilton holds an unprecedented seven Formula One World Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record, while leading in multiple statistical categories including race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances. Since 2025, Hamilton has joined Ferrari after spending his previous years with other competitive teams, continuing his pursuit of further success at the sport's highest level.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg is a German racing driver currently competing in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved significant success in endurance racing, securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver Charles Leclerc currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured multiple Grand Prix victories throughout his nine-year tenure in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW through WRT, while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career with Trackhouse Racing. His Formula One career spanned two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: British driver Lando Norris claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren, adding to his career tally of 12 Grand Prix victories accumulated over eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The skilled competitor achieved his sole Grand Prix victory during the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio "Checo" Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after spending 15 seasons competing at the sport's highest level. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri represents Australia in Formula One competition with McLaren, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-year stint in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo is an Australian driver who participated in Formula One racing over a 14-year span from 2011 through 2024, accumulating eight Grand Prix victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," Ricciardo has since retired from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Vázquez de Castro currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has claimed four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously contested IMSA's LMP2 division. He competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to his present endurance racing commitments.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently competing in Formula One with Aston Martin as his racing team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda held a Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 and currently functions as a reserve driver for both Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch driver Max Verstappen currently races for Red Bull Racing, where he has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. With 71 race victories accumulated over twelve seasons in Formula One, Verstappen stands as one of the sport's most successful modern competitors.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, the sole Chinese competitor in Formula One history, raced in the series from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve driver role with Cadillac. His career represents a significant milestone as the first and only driver from China to participate at the sport's highest level.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, representing Renault's rebranding of its works Formula One operation before the manufacturer's 2025 departure from the sport. Operating under French licensing with Mercedes power units, the team achieved its only Alpine-era victory through Esteban Ocon's triumph at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive company, has maintained an on-and-off presence in Formula One across different organizational structures, with its current incarnation competing under the AMR GP Limited banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, holds the distinction of being both the longest-running and most accomplished team in Formula One history, with continuous participation since the championship's inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially referred to as "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, remains synonymous with the sport's heritage and competitive excellence.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, debuting on the grid in 2016 with backing from Toyota. Ayao Komatsu assumed the team principal role in 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who led the outfit since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: The Swiss engineering firm, established by Peter Sauber in 1970, initially built sports cars before transitioning to single-seater construction and competing in Formula One from 1993 onwards. The operation achieved endurance racing success including a Le Mans victory, though its F1 tenure ended in 2025 as one of the sport's most established independent constructors. Audi acquired the operation in 2024 to serve as the foundation for its factory team programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking, operating as a subsidiary within the McLaren Group. The team competes under corporate sponsorship arrangements and is ultimately owned by Bahraini investment firm Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 through team ownership and engine supply. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas squad, operating from Brackley with a German licence, underwent a significant ownership restructure in 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal stakeholder alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff. The team is traditionally known by the "Silver Arrows" moniker.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team operates as the second constructor under the Austrian conglomerate's Formula One portfolio.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates alongside Red Bull Racing as the conglomerate's second racing entity in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England, owned by the Red Bull conglomerate alongside Racing Bulls. Founded in 2005 and led by Christian Horner until 2025, the team has since been placed under the direction of Laurent Mekies.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerged following the failure of Williams's initial F1 venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 championship as Atlassian Williams F1 Team.
